patch_description: Builds on the strongest prior candidate (even/odd shared RY rotations + shared ring/long-range entanglers + shared global RZ phase, which scored 0.52) by restructuring the entangling layers so that, together, they cover every pairwise qubit distance (1,2,3,4) on the 8-qubit ring — i.e. a complete graph K8 — while still using only two distinct entangling parameter names. Distance-1/2 edges share a single IsingZZ parameter ("zz_ring") and distance-3/4 edges share a single CRZ parameter ("crz_long"), so the trainable parameter count stays the same as the current best (5 distinct circuit parameters + 2 readout = 7 total) but the fixed (non-trainable) connectivity is now maximal. This exploits the stated principle that "sharing is the only way to reduce parameter count without removing gates" in the constructive direction: adding much richer fixed structure without paying any parameter-count cost. Full all-to-all entanglement, replicated across the 3 repeated blocks with tied parameters, should let the small parameter budget carve out more robust decision boundaries (better worst-group margin) since every readout pair is reachable through short, densely-shared interaction chains instead of relying on diffusion around a sparse ring. The even/odd split for local RY rotations is kept unchanged since it was empirically the key ingredient that lifted the score from ~0.36-0.38 to 0.52.
